target_customer: Cardiologists and hospitals treating chronic heart failure patients
problem: Fluid overload drives symptoms and hospitalizations in heart failure; the MILO device offloads fluid in a one time minimally invasive procedure.
business_model: Medical device sold to hospitals (pre-revenue, not sourced)

founders.name: Stacie Arechavala
education: Duke, master's in biomedical engineering and engineering management

founders.name: Kevin Bui
prior_employers: Stanford Byers Center for Biodesign (innovation fellow)

competitors.name: Corvia Medical
competitors.what: Interatrial shunt implant that decompresses the left atrium in heart failure
competitors.traction_then: Two year REDUCE LAP-HF II data reported May 2023; CE mark in EU

competitors.name: Alleviant Medical
competitors.traction_then: Early human data in 2022; sham controlled ALLAY-HFrEF trial planned

technical_complexity.rationale: A catheter based implant that manages fluid via the body's fluid system needs device development, clinical evidence and regulatory clearance.

defensibility.rationale: Device patents and approval pathways would raise barriers, but no patents or trial data are sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rival shunt makers were in trials; a May 2024 acquisition claim on a directory is unverified and unsupported.

market_need_then: Heart failure affects millions and fluid overload drives hospitalizations (company claim); rival shunt trials show device interest.

branding.domain_note: seleramedical.com showed an under construction placeholder.

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes the logo, visual style or voice, so the brand cannot be rated above forgettable.

outcome_analysis: Selera Medical was a Stanford Biodesign alumni startup developing the MILO one time heart failure device, in YC Winter 2024. The YC directory lists it as Inactive and its website is a coming soon placeholder, yet no shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. A single directory claims an acquisition in May 2024 without naming a buyer and that claim is not supported. Medical device timelines and capital needs are a likely but unsourced constraint.
notes: Round rests on Caplight (investors) plus FundedIQ and VCBacked (amount, April 2024). Another directory (sp-edge) claims an acquisition in May 2024, unverified, so exit is unknown. YesPress could not be opened (HTTP 403).
